about.expert_notes: Continuous: PIT = P(ŷ < y) + ½ P(ŷ = y); the line is ECDF(z) − z on a grid of min(max(n, 20), 200) points. The simultaneous envelope at `prob` (0.95) is ±c·sqrt(z(1−z)/n) with c the `prob` quantile of the largest standardised deviation over the grid in `n_sim` (1000) simulated uniform samples (cumulative multinomial counts, `seed`). Binary (auto when y ∈ {0, 1} and the draws are in [0, 1]): `bins` (10) equal-width bins of the mean prediction; each band is the binomial range p ± z·sqrt(p(1−p)/n_bin); the expected calibration error weights |observed − predicted| by bin size. A point prediction (no sample dims, values in [0, 1], for example the y_hat of an sklearn classifier) takes the binary path with the probability as the mean; `var` and `observed_var` pick the pair. A point prediction of a target that is not 0/1 is an error, because the PIT check needs draws.

The values in the log_likelihood group are in the same order as the actual values

about.expert_notes: PSIS (Vehtari et al. 2024) on the log ratios −log p(y_i | θ_s): tail length M = ceil(min(0.2 S, 3 √S)), a generalized Pareto fit (Zhang and Stephens, with the weakly informative prior) whose quantiles replace the tail, truncated at the largest raw weight; k = inf when the tail is too short. LOO-PIT_i = Σ_s w_si 1[ŷ_si < y_i] + ½ Σ_s w_si 1[ŷ_si = y_i] with the normalised weights. The envelope is the simultaneous one of Calibration (`prob` 0.95, `n_sim` 1000, `seed`).
